RSA Keys

Source: R/pkey.R
crypt_rsa_keys.Rd

Read, write, generate and take apart RSA keys. The names, arguments and defaults follow the openssl package with a crypt_ prefix, and the encodings interoperate: a key one package writes, the other reads.

  • crypt_read_key() reads a private key and crypt_read_pubkey() a public key, from PEM or DER: PKCS#1, PKCS#8 or SubjectPublicKeyInfo. crypt_read_pubkey() also accepts a private key and keeps its public half.

  • crypt_write_pem() writes PKCS#8 (PRIVATE KEY) or SubjectPublicKeyInfo (PUBLIC KEY) PEM; crypt_write_pkcs1() writes PKCS#1 PEM (RSA PRIVATE KEY, RSA PUBLIC KEY); crypt_write_der() writes a private key as PKCS#1 DER and a public key as SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, as openssl::write_der() does.

  • crypt_rsa_keygen() generates a key pair from the operating system's random source.

  • crypt_rsa_key() builds a key from its integers, as a JSON Web Key carries them, and as.list() takes one apart again.

A key object is an external pointer to key material held in C, and the material of a private key is wiped when the object is garbage collected. Key objects do not survive saveRDS(); save the PEM instead.

Usage

crypt_read_key(file, password = NULL, der = is.raw(file))

crypt_read_pubkey(file, der = is.raw(file))

crypt_rsa_keygen(bits = 2048)

crypt_write_pem(x, path = NULL, password = NULL)

crypt_write_der(x, path = NULL)

crypt_write_pkcs1(x, path = NULL, password = NULL)

crypt_rsa_key(
  n,
  e,
  d = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  q = NULL,
  dp = NULL,
  dq = NULL,
  qi = NULL
)

Arguments

file

The key: a raw vector of DER or PEM bytes, a single string of PEM text, a path to a file holding either, or a connection.

password

Not supported yet: password-protected keys arrive in a later version. Must be NULL.

der

Accepted for compatibility with openssl; the encoding is recognised from the content.

bits

The modulus size, a multiple of 8 from 1024 to 4096. 2048 is the minimum for new keys; use 3072 or more for keys meant to last.

x

A key from crypt_read_key(), crypt_read_pubkey(), crypt_rsa_keygen() or crypt_rsa_key().

path

NULL to return the encoding, or a file to write it to.

n, e

The modulus and the public exponent, as raw big-endian unsigned integers.

d, p, q, dp, dq, qi

The private exponent, the primes and the CRT parameters, as raw big-endian unsigned integers. Give all six for a private key, or none for a public key.

Value

crypt_read_key(), crypt_rsa_keygen() and crypt_rsa_key() with the private members return a key of class c("crypt_key", "crypt_rsa"); crypt_read_pubkey() and crypt_rsa_key() without them return one of class c("crypt_pubkey", "crypt_rsa"). crypt_write_pem() and crypt_write_pkcs1() return a string, and crypt_write_der() a raw vector, or with path write it and return path invisibly. as.list() returns type, size, for a private key pubkey, and data: the integers as raw vectors, e, n and for a private key p, q, d, dp, dq and qi.

Errors

Input that is not a readable key is zucrypt_invalid_argument, and so is a public key object given where a private key is needed. A well-formed key this version cannot use (an RSA key outside the size rule, a curve other than P-256, P-384 and P-521, or an encrypted key) is zucrypt_unsupported_algorithm. A condition about a key carries the key's type in its algorithm field ("rsa", "p256", "p384", "p521" or "x25519"), and NA when the input is not a key.

Key objects

A key object refers to key material held outside R, so a copy is the same key, not a new one: changing the attributes of k2 <- k changes k too. Key objects do not survive saveRDS(); save the output of crypt_write_pem() instead.

Compared with openssl

RSA keys are read only if the modulus is 1024 to 4096 bits, a whole number of bytes; openssl also reads smaller keys, which are weak, and larger ones. EC keys on P-256, P-384 and P-521, and X25519 keys, are read as openssl writes them. Encrypted keys, SSH formats and fingerprints come later. as.list() gives the integers as raw vectors rather than bignums. There is no default key: openssl reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa, and this package never reads your files unless you name them.

Examples

key <- crypt_rsa_keygen(2048)
key
#> [2048-bit rsa private key]
pem <- crypt_write_pem(key$pubkey)
cat(pem)
#> -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
#> MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAzXpFQ3JZB/VJs/b1Khgk
#> NQn1pOf8lFASMPeszlGkDluhpW35atQiKpYKnAUqVJHALNOXJxLFZGc0R2Sh8Erc
#> hhJbRZgpdQIfTHRPlgrvizKGd1IaDqwaJI8Oa8UxJI8hwlAD/Z+qZbyiQiLkiB49
#> wtp87SNFug6s6/9t3b0yver2Lpm3bldZWpBP91iuFPXRgok+lZPd5aBQJYtTxl+P
#> /om8+dHKrDlOOdBkgWxQb8jpazhoQ1k2YjGEgWSAq0PMOuKDrM+3WWIbAkrhwk2A
#> ffF3ZIt6ZfEUPMEAExOqYH2C1LrLZF25Hx4J31xfoHjBhRe1cy1dCEp6gq+BKAhl
#> 9wIDAQAB
#> -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
pub <- crypt_read_pubkey(pem)

# The integers a JSON Web Key carries, and back.
parts <- as.list(pub)$data
identical(crypt_write_der(crypt_rsa_key(parts$n, parts$e)),
          crypt_write_der(pub))
#> [1] TRUE
